definition.text: Scope neglect is a cognitive bias in which the value people place on a problem does not grow in proportion to its size.

facts.text: In one study people were willing to pay $80, $78 and $88 to save 2,000, 20,000 or 200,000 migrating birds from drowning in oil ponds.
Other willingness-to-pay studies have found a logarithmic relationship or no relationship to the size of the harm.
Daniel Kahneman explains it as judgment by prototype: people price a mental image, such as one oil-soaked bird, rather than the number affected.
It is a specific form of extension neglect, closely linked to the 'mass numbing' studied by Paul Slovic.
